ordered_diagnoses: Congenital granular cell tumor of the tongue

facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old man
no significant medical history
a 1.5-cm diameter, exophytic, smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue
the lesion had been present since birth and had not changed in size or character
Vital signs were within normal limits
An MRI of the tongue showed a 1.5-cm protuberant mass arising from the dorsal aspect of the tongue in the midline at the junction of the oral component and base
the lesion appeared partly fatty, likely submucosal, demonstrated mild contrast enhancement, had intact overlying mucosa, and showed no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles
the sublingual space and major salivary glands appeared normal

concepts.preferred_label: Congenital granular cell tumor of the tongue
concepts.why: The presence of a congenital, exophytic, and partly fatty lesion on the dorsal tongue, with intact overlying mucosa and no involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles, is consistent with a congenital granular cell tumor.
The location and appearance of the lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue, combined with its smooth and regular shape, could be consistent with a lingual thyroid.
The presence of a congenital, exophytic lesion on the dorsal tongue, with a partly fatty appearance, could be consistent with a dermoid cyst.
The partly fatty appearance of the lesion, combined with its smooth and regular shape, could be consistent with a lipoma of the tongue.
The presence of a congenital, exophytic lesion on the dorsal tongue, with a smooth and regular shape, could be consistent with a hamartoma.

rationales.F03: The presence of a smooth, regular, and soft lesion on the midline of the dorsal tongue is consistent with several tongue lesions.
rationales.F04: The long-standing nature of the lesion suggests a congenital or benign condition.
rationales.F07: The partly fatty composition and lack of involvement of intrinsic tongue muscles are highly suggestive of a lipoma or congenital granular cell tumor.
rationales.F08: The normal appearance of the sublingual space and major salivary glands makes lingual thyroid less likely.

frontier_selector.runner_up: Congenital granular cell tumor of the tongue
frontier_selector.rationale: The lesion's partly fatty appearance and submucosal location, as shown on MRI, are most consistent with a lipoma, a benign tumor composed of fat tissue.
